commits.message:
test(seam): make host access a checked list, not four claims (rich-seam-981.6) (#75)

* test(seam): make host access a checked list, not four claims (rich-seam-981.6)

Four comments claimed who owns node TTY access and no two agreed on the
scope. `docs/widgets.md` said `NodeTerminalHost` "is the only thing that
touches `process.stdin` and `process.stdout`" — false; `src/node/prompt.ts`
reads both. The three in `src/` survived only by narrowing until they no
longer overlapped their counterexamples, and none of the four mentioned
`prompt.ts` at all, because none of them was checked.

`HOST_ACCESS` in `test/seam/ambient-process.ts` is now the one home: every
file in `src/` that reads the ambient `process`, the property names it takes,
and a required `why`. The gate fails when a file joins the list without an
entry and when an entry outlives the read it was granted for. Granularity is
per-property on purpose — it is what let the scan answer the question the
narrowed sentences were circling, and answer it against them: there is no
sole reader of `process.stdin`, there are two, and what is true is that both
sit behind `package.json#exports` subpaths.

Not the browser-safety rule next door, though both scan for the same
identifier. That one asks whether a module-scope read throws when a browser
evaluates the barrel; this one asks what the package takes off the host in
any scope. A function-body leak passes there and fails here — pinned from
both sides by a fixture in each suite. `isNameSlot` moves to
`test/seam/identifiers.ts` so the two rules share it rather than drift.

The prose now points at the list instead of restating it.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012UgGnaLFsGbmjXrjHGkhea

* fix(seam): prune type queries as a subtree, not by parent kind

`type T = typeof process.env` reported a whole-object host read. The
identifier's parent there is the `QualifiedName`, not the `TypeQueryNode`,
so matching on the parent saw nothing — while the function's own doc
comment promised a `typeof` takes nothing off the host. Pruning the query's
subtree covers every spelling of it at once and retires the parent-kind
clause; type positions are otherwise still walked, which is the deliberate
difference from `browser-safe.ts`.

`docs/widgets.md` stops naming the two stream members. A published page is
the wrong place to send a reader into `test/seam/`, but enumerating what
`HOST_ACCESS` enumerates is the drift this PR exists to remove — so the
member list goes and the claims that remain are ones the suite pins.
